item.title: [Critical] Bloomberg: hackers reached tanker VL Prosperity’s propulsion system — the FBI reports no disruption and no attacker is named
item.category: Top Story
item.description: On 2 October Bloomberg, citing unnamed US officials, reported that FBI and Coast Guard investigators found hackers had accessed the propulsion system of the crude supertanker VL Prosperity as it neared the Texas coast this summer. Neither agency has confirmed that on the record, and how long the access lasted, or what it could control, is unknown. The FBI says it has no reports of operational disruption, vessel instability, danger to crews or environmental harm. The confirmed part dates from September: cyber teams boarded two foreign-flagged, US-bound energy tankers in August after signs their networks were compromised, which the Coast Guard attributes to foreign cyber actors. Per Dragos, VL Prosperity was boarded on 21 August in the Atlantic and the second, unnamed tanker on 24 August in the Gulf of Mexico. No new official statement had been found by 16 October. For terminal operators, the exposure is the ship-shore interface. - Bloomberg report of 2 Oct 2026, as syndicated by gCaptain and SupplyChainBrain, citing unnamed US officials, with the FBI’s on-record statement; joint US Coast Guard and FBI statement via CyberScoop and The Record; Rear Adm. Grable via CBS News; boarding locations per Dragos (“VL Prosperity: What MTSA Cybersecurity Already Requires”, 24 Sep 2026); engine-room claims trace to Iranian state media and are unverified; the second vessel has not been named by the agencies - Boardings 21 and 24 Aug 2026; publicly confirmed 16 Sep 2026; Dragos commentary 24 Sep 2026; Bloomberg propulsion-system report 2 Oct 2026, not confirmed on the record; Baird Maritime recap 7 Oct 2026; no new official statement found to 16 Oct 2026

item.title: [High] FBI and Secret Service: the FortiBleed credential campaign against FortiGate firewalls is still running — and the energy sector is among its targets
item.category: Active campaign — FBI and Secret Service warning on FortiGate credential theft; energy among targeted sectors; no CVE; no OT compromise described
item.description: In a joint advisory dated Tuesday 6 October (JCSA-20261006-01), the FBI and US Secret Service warned that the FortiBleed campaign against internet-facing Fortinet FortiGate firewalls and SSL VPN gateways remains an active threat, with attackers still scanning for devices they can log into using credentials obtained earlier. There is no CVE: the agencies describe abuse of reused or leaked credentials and of legacy SHA-256 password storage. Researcher reporting adds credential stuffing and spraying from leak dumps, offline cracking of extracted hashes and a tool, FortigateSniffer, that passively captures authentication traffic across 24 protocols. Intruders have created administrator accounts with names such as fortiAdmin, forticloud-sync and fgtsecure, and some owners were locked out after attackers reset or deleted the legitimate accounts. The agencies say targets span all 16 US critical infrastructure sectors, energy and food and agriculture among them, and the FBI links the access to Payload ransomware; SOCRadar says it has confirmed at least 12 ransomware deployments that began this way. SOCRadar’s figure of 86,644 working device credentials in 194 countries dates from 19 June and is not a new count. Researchers describe the operator as a Russian-speaking initial access broker whose buyers overlap with INC and Lynx affiliates; that is their assessment, not the agencies’. No OT system compromise has been described and no oil and gas victim named. The sector read is ours: FortiGate is one of the most common firewalls at the IT/OT boundary and at remote sites, so a working login on one is a step toward operations. - FBI and US Secret Service joint advisory JCSA-20261006-01 (6 Oct 2026), as reported by Cybersecurity Dive and The Hacker News (7 Oct 2026); ransomware counts, credential figures and the operator profile are SOCRadar and researcher assessments; oil and gas relevance is editorial assessment - Campaign first documented June 2026; agency warning 6 Oct 2026; reported 7 Oct 2026

item.title: [Medium] CenterPoint Energy tells Texas its customer-data breach reached 1,062,060 residents — and still says gas and electric operations were not affected
item.category: Incident — Customer data breach at a gas and electric utility, now more than 1 million Texans; no operational impact
item.description: CenterPoint Energy, the Houston-based electric and natural gas utility, has told the Texas Attorney General’s Office that 1,062,060 Texas residents were affected by the breach it disclosed in September, SecurityWeek reported on 15 October. As SecurityWeek describes the filing, the exposed data includes names, addresses, Social Security numbers and driver’s licence numbers; residents of Indiana, Minnesota and Ohio may also be affected, and no overall total has been given. The company again says the incident did not affect its operations. In its SEC filing CenterPoint said an unauthorised party obtained customer information through one of its external-facing systems and that it learned of the breach from the actor’s own public post; BleepingComputer reported in September that the system was a public API with no rate limiting, web application firewall or automated access controls. The actor claimed nearly 7.5 million records and posted a 2.5 GB archive on 12 September; the company has not confirmed that figure, and class-action filings allege the intrusion ran from 17 August to 1 September. This is an IT and customer-data incident, not an OT one, and it is scored that way. It belongs on an oil and gas page because gas distribution utilities run customer-facing APIs alongside SCADA for pressure and flow, and the useful question is how much those two estates share. - CenterPoint Energy filing with the Texas Attorney General’s Office, as reported by SecurityWeek (15 Oct 2026); SEC filing and API detail as reported by BleepingComputer and The Record in September; record count claimed by the actor, not confirmed by the company - Intrusion alleged 17 Aug–1 Sep 2026; company disclosure 15 Sep 2026; Texas filing reported 15 Oct 2026

item.title: [Medium] The Vivit Africa LNG crew’s claim that attackers took control of safety-valve, tank-pressure and boil-off systems is still unverified — the Italian Coast Guard records a cargo-monitoring malfunction of undetermined cause
item.category: Incident — Suspected; crew claims control of safety systems, unverified; cause officially undetermined
item.description: Bloomberg first reported on 18 September that the crew lost access to some internal control systems in early September as the ship approached the Adriatic. On 21 September Splash247 published the account the crew of Vivit Africa LNG sent to the outlet and, it says, to Korean Register, the ship’s class society. The crew claims that attackers gained temporary control of the steam-pressure and safety-valve systems while the ship transited the Strait of Gibraltar, and later, in the Adriatic, of tank-pressure control, pressure-relief valves and boil-off gas management — which they say significantly increased the risk of tank rupture and explosion. Splash247 states plainly that it has not independently verified the claims, and no other party has confirmed them. The official record is narrower. Italian Coast Guard Capt. Roberto D’Arrigo says the master reported “a malfunction in the systems used to monitor cargo parameters” that required company technicians, that the cause “could not be identified”, and that the Coast Guard issued a navigational warning and intervened only for safety of navigation. Kongsberg Maritime, which supplies equipment aboard, said on 18 September it was too early to draw conclusions about the cause or any security implications; Vitol, the charterer, declined to comment beyond confirming the charter, and H-Line Shipping, the owner, and Korean Register have not responded. What is confirmed is the movement: the vessel loaded at Cameron LNG in Louisiana for the Adriatic LNG terminal near Rovigo, idled off Italy without discharging, then abandoned the call and sailed west toward Algeciras. Bloomberg counts it as the third tanker in about a month after the two US-bound vessels boarded by the Coast Guard and FBI, but no agency has linked the cases. Until an investigator, the class society or the equipment supplier reports, this remains a suspected incident with an unverified crew claim attached — and it is scored that way; with nothing new found by 16 October, this edition keeps it at Medium. For oil and gas the relevance is unchanged: a US LNG export cargo, and the cargo-monitoring and tank-pressure functions that are the shipboard counterpart of terminal custody-transfer, loading and ESD data. - Crew account published by Splash247, which states it has not verified it; Bloomberg report (gCaptain repost) with Italian Coast Guard, Korean Register and Kongsberg statements as quoted; vessel movements per Bloomberg and Marine Insight; cause undetermined, no attribution - Incident early Sep 2026; first reported 18 Sep 2026; crew claims published 21 Sep 2026; no new development found as of 16 Oct 2026, and still unconfirmed by any authority, class society or supplier

item.title: [High] The FBI seizes domains behind Microscan and FishHub, China-linked tools whose targets included gas and power companies — no OT intrusion is described
item.category: Threat Intelligence — US seizure of China-linked scanning and phishing tooling; gas and power companies among named targets; no compromise of those targets confirmed
item.description: On 8 October the Justice Department and FBI announced court-authorised seizures, in the Western District of Pennsylvania, of domains used to run two tools: Microscan, a Python web application with more than 1,300 penetration-testing scripts, supported by a Mirai-variant IoT botnet, and FishHub, used for spear-phishing and malware delivery. US authorities tie the tooling to China-based Integrity Technology Group, the company sanctioned last year and linked to a 2024 botnet takedown. The attribution wording varies: CyberScoop calls the tools Flax Typhoon-linked, while Cybersecurity Dive says the company’s activity mimics that of the group tracked as Flax Typhoon rather than equating the two. Court documents, as Cybersecurity Dive reports them, list Microscan targets including a South Carolina power company, airports in Japan and Poland, a multinational NGO, and gas and power companies in Taiwan; FishHub was aimed at Taiwanese universities. None of those targets has been confirmed as compromised. A joint FBI, CISA and NSA advisory accompanied the seizures, and CISA’s Chris Butera said China-affiliated actors continue to position themselves inside critical infrastructure networks, OT systems included. No operational impact is described. For oil and gas the link is direct rather than inferred: gas companies were on the target list of a state-linked scanning platform, and scanning is the stage that comes before access. - DOJ and FBI announcement and joint FBI, CISA and NSA advisory, as reported by CyberScoop (8 Oct 2026) and Cybersecurity Dive (9 Oct 2026); target list from court documents as reported; attribution wording differs between outlets; oil and gas relevance is editorial assessment - Seizures announced 8 Oct 2026

item.title: [Medium] Attackers forced defrost on refrigeration controllers in about 700 French supermarkets — a food-sector attack, and a test for every vendor-managed controller you expose
item.category: Cross-sector lesson — confirmed OT attack on supermarket refrigeration controllers in France; not an oil and gas incident; sector link is editorial assessment
item.description: Over the nights of 11–13 October, the second wave hitting stores with Dixell equipment, attackers remotely changed settings on web-managed refrigeration controllers in French supermarkets, forcing extended defrost cycles that pushed cabinets toward about 50°C and spoiled stock; the Paris prosecutor reports fires at some sites. Finance Minister Roland Lescure told Parliament on 13 October that roughly 700 of France’s 10,000 supermarkets were hit, across Carrefour, Coopérative U, E.Leclerc, Intermarché and Netto, and Monoprix. CERT-FR’s alert CERTFR-2026-ALE-012 named Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC controllers on 12 October, added Copeland and Dixell xweb on 13 October, and on 16 October said the campaigns are probably still under way. No actor has claimed it, no ransom has been demanded and the entry route has not been established; Danfoss and Copeland say most affected units are older, end-of-life models. Two follow-ups reach beyond retail. Nozomi Networks’ 13 October analysis links the same precondition — controllers left reachable from the internet for vendor management — to fuel automatic tank gauges, citing Shadowserver’s count of 909 exposed gauges in June. And Claroty Team82 reported on 13 October that an AI coding agent, redirected by a human, reproduced a previously disclosed Danfoss AK-SM 800A authentication-bypass and command-injection chain to root on a lab device in about 28 minutes for roughly $6; Team82 does not say those flaws were used in France. This is not an oil and gas incident and it does not count toward this page’s score. The lesson is ours: tank gauges, forecourt and convenience-store refrigeration, building management and vendor-monitored packages at terminals and retail fuel sites belong to the same exposure class. - CERT-FR alert CERTFR-2026-ALE-012 (v1 12 Oct, v2 13 Oct, v3 16 Oct 2026); Finance Minister Lescure via AP (13 Oct 2026); affected chains per SecurityWeek (15 Oct 2026); Nozomi Networks analysis and Claroty Team82 research (13 Oct 2026); exposure counts are third-party figures; oil and gas relevance is editorial assessment - Attacks on the nights of 11–13 Oct 2026; CERT-FR alert updated 16 Oct 2026

item.title: [Low] Dragos: old worms such as Conficker, Sality and WannaCry keep turning up in OT incident calls — and the wrong cleanup can do more harm than the infection
item.category: Research — Commodity malware in OT networks and how to clean it up; vendor guidance, no actor
item.description: Dragos’s Lesley Carhart and Jan Hoff wrote on 15 October that requests for help with legacy commodity infections — Sality, Gammima, WannaCry and Conficker among them — have risen sharply in recent years. Many OT networks Dragos is called into carry between 20 and 70 distinct commodity-malware variants spread across several subnets, often on systems older than Windows XP SP2. They put the rise down to more networking and remote access, better visibility, and regulation that expects critical-infrastructure networks to be clean. Their answer is a triage framework they call Now, Next and Never, published with a white paper, and a warning that a cleanup done the wrong way can be riskier than the infection it is meant to remove. There is no CVE and no actor here. The fit for oil and gas is our assessment and an easy one: refineries, gas plants and pipeline control centres keep operator stations, historians and vendor PCs on old Windows builds for years, and an aggressive cleanup — mass reboots, forced updates or an endpoint agent pushed onto running units — can stop a process the worm never touched. - Dragos blog by Lesley Carhart and Jan Hoff (15 Oct 2026), with its linked white paper; oil and gas application is editorial assessment - Published 15 Oct 2026

item.title: [Medium] Symantec: the China-nexus group behind Warlock ransomware broke into a water utility and a telecom operator through on-premises SharePoint — no OT impact is described, and no energy victim is named
item.category: Threat Intelligence — China-nexus ransomware intrusions via SharePoint; water and telecom victims; cross-sector context, no OT impact described
item.description: Symantec’s Threat Hunter Team reported on 1 October that a group it calls Longlegs, which it describes as a China-nexus threat actor also tracked as Storm-2603, has attacked at least four organisations in the past two months: two critical infrastructure operators — a water utility and a telecommunications provider — plus a regional government body and a university, in Portuguese- and Spanish-speaking countries in Europe, Africa and Latin America. No victim or country is named. Symantec says the group typically gets in by exploiting several vulnerabilities in on-premises Microsoft SharePoint Server; the CVEs it names are the 2025 ToolShell flaws (CVE-2025-49704, CVE-2025-49706, CVE-2025-53770 and CVE-2025-53771), alongside unspecified related SharePoint flaws. Once inside, the group steals ASP.NET machine keys, sideloads DLLs, uses Visual Studio Code tunnels and NetExec, and loads a vulnerable signed driver (CVE-2025-1055 in K7RKScan) to switch off security tools; in one intrusion Symantec documents, Warlock was pushed to at least 33 hosts through SYSVOL. Symantec does not describe any operational or OT impact at the water utility and does not say ransomware was deployed there. It is on this page as cross-sector context, not an oil and gas incident: the targets are critical infrastructure operators, the entry point is the kind of on-premises collaboration server that engineering and document-control teams often run, and machine-key theft means a server patched after compromise can still be reopened. - Symantec Threat Hunter Team report, with coverage by BleepingComputer and SecurityWeek; attribution and victim descriptions are Symantec’s; oil and gas relevance is editorial assessment - Published 1 Oct 2026; intrusions over the preceding two months

item.title: [Medium] Recorded Future: Russia’s hybrid pressure on Europe is “largely opportunistic” for now — and a drone intercepted near Romania’s Neptun Deep offshore gas field is among its cases
item.category: Threat Intelligence — Nation-state hybrid threat assessment; physical and cyber; no new OT impact
item.description: Recorded Future’s Insikt Group published an assessment on 24 September that Russia has escalated what it calls “New Generation Warfare” tactics in Europe since February 2022, combining sabotage, drones, cyber operations and disinformation. It judges current activity “largely opportunistic”, but likely to escalate over the next two years, potentially culminating in a full-scale campaign. The incidents it cites include an explosive maritime drone intercepted near Romania’s Neptun Deep offshore gas field on 20 August 2026, a sabotage plot using military-grade explosives against cargo infrastructure at Leipzig/Halle Airport in August, DDoS and access operations against the Norwegian public sector on 30 August, and subsea cables as a growing target. Dark Reading’s coverage adds that the research cites water and wastewater targeting in Norway and Poland and attacks on Poland’s energy infrastructure in early 2026. Insikt’s recommendations include contractor and insider vetting, perimeter detection and anti-drone measures, alternative supply routes, coordination with national CERTs and phishing-resistant MFA. This is an analytic assessment attributed to Russia at assessment level; the blog names no specific unit and reports no new OT process impact. It is separate from the ENISA threat landscape below. For operators with European offshore, pipeline and terminal assets the relevance is direct: the physical and cyber threats are being assessed together, so the security planning for those assets should be too. - Recorded Future Insikt Group blog (24 Sep 2026), with additional detail as reported by Dark Reading; attribution is Insikt’s assessment; oil and gas application is editorial assessment - Published 24 Sep 2026; Neptun Deep drone intercept 20 Aug 2026

item.title: [Medium] Microsoft profiles Storm-2570, a ransomware affiliate that switches between Qilin, DragonForce, Anubis and BERT while its tradecraft stays the same — energy and chemicals are on its victim list
item.category: Threat Intelligence — Ransomware affiliate tradecraft; energy and chemicals among victim sectors; IT-side, no OT impact reported
item.description: Microsoft Threat Intelligence published a profile on 24 September of Storm-2570, a ransomware affiliate it has tracked since April 2025 that has deployed Qilin, DragonForce, Anubis and BERT ransomware. Microsoft lists victims in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Spain, the Netherlands and Puerto Rico, in sectors that include energy, chemicals, critical manufacturing and transportation as well as healthcare, education, government and financial services. It says the method of initial access “remains unconfirmed”. The tooling is mostly legitimate software: remote-management agents including Atera, MeshAgent, ScreenConnect, Splashtop and NinjaRMM; PsExec, Impacket and NetExec for lateral movement; Mimikatz, LaZagne and ntdsutil for credentials; ngrok and Cloudflare tunnels; and Rclone and s5cmd for exfiltration. Microsoft names no individual victim and describes no OT impact. Two points carry over to oil and gas. Switching ransomware brands changes the leak site, not the behaviour, so detections built on behaviour — a new RMM agent, PsExec from an unusual host, an ntdsutil run — keep working when the brand changes. And the same RMM tools are common in vendor support for plant, pipeline and terminal systems, which makes an allow-list of approved remote tools an OT control as well as an IT one. - Microsoft Threat Intelligence blog (24 Sep 2026), reviewed directly; no victims named; oil and gas application is editorial assessment - Published 24 Sep 2026

item.title: [Medium] Forescout: only 13% of network segments with OT devices are OT-only — and oil and gas is among the three sectors with the largest average “blast radius”
item.category: Research — Network segmentation exposure analysis
item.description: Forescout Vedere Labs published an analysis on 22 September of 47,700 network segments containing more than 2.5 million devices at 209 organisations. Its headline finding: “Of all segments containing OT devices, 13% are OT-only”; the other 87% also hold other types of device. Forescout measures “blast radius” as the number of devices that share a segment, which is roughly how far an attacker can reach from one compromised device without crossing a control. Forescout names business and professional services, healthcare, and oil and gas as the sectors with “the largest average ‘blast radius’”, while utilities, financial services and retail have the lowest; Industrial Cyber’s report of the study puts the oil and gas average at 72 devices per segment. Its recommendations are continuous asset visibility, identifying and prioritising “device convergence zones”, separating critical operational assets from enterprise IT, reducing oversized segments, policy-based access control between segments, and monitoring for segmentation drift. This is exposure data from one vendor’s dataset, not an incident, and it does not name organisations. It does describe the condition that turns an exploited edge device, like those in this edition’s KEV cards, into an OT problem. - Forescout Vedere Labs research blog (22 Sep 2026), reviewed directly; also reported by SecurityWeek; oil and gas per-segment average as reported by Industrial Cyber; oil and gas application is editorial assessment - Published 22 Sep 2026

item.title: [Medium] NCC Group counts 1,073 ransomware attacks in August, a 2026 high, with the industrial sector bearing 31% — and energy incidents are still landing on IT, which is where the outage comes from
item.category: Threat Intelligence & Research — Ransomware statistics
item.description: NCC Group’s review of August 2026, reported by Industrial Cyber on 28 September, counts 1,073 ransomware attacks, up 12 percent from 960 in July. The industrial sector accounted for 329 of them, about 31 percent, and North America for 473, about 44 percent. Qilin led with 164 claimed attacks, overtaking The Gentlemen. NCC also describes Aurora, a ransomware-as-a-service group active since late April that goes after manufacturing, legal, research and transportation organisations through weak or unauthenticated VPN access before encrypting hypervisors. A different tracker, Comparitech, reported on 14 September a record 997 attacks for the same month; the counts differ because each tracker has its own method, and both rest largely on leak-site claims, so a claimed victim is not a confirmed one, and neither breaks out oil and gas. The pattern they fit is the one the sector already knows from Colonial Pipeline onward — encryption lands on business systems, and operations stop because scheduling, billing, custody-transfer accounting or terminal ticketing depends on them, not because anything touched a controller. - NCC Group’s monthly ransomware review, reported by Industrial Cyber; Comparitech tracking, reported by Industrial Cyber; both counts rest largely on actor claims and do not break out oil and gas - Data for August 2026; Comparitech figures reported 14 Sep 2026; NCC Group figures reported 28 Sep 2026

item.title: [High] Nozomi chains 12 flaws in the Siemens SCALANCE LPE9403 to root on an OT edge device — patched, and not exploited
item.category: Research — OT edge device, vendor-patched vulnerability chain
item.description: Nozomi Networks Labs published the second part of its Siemens SCALANCE LPE9403 research on 18 September: twelve vulnerabilities in total, nine in the device firmware and three in the SINEMA Remote Connect Edge Client. Firmware below V4.0 HF0 and Edge Client releases through V2.1 are affected, and Siemens has published an advisory with fixes in V4.0 HF0 and later. Nozomi demonstrated that several of the flaws can be chained to obtain root-level control of the device, which would allow manipulation of telemetry, suppression of alarms, access to operational data, disruption of edge services and lateral movement into the networks the device sits between. There is no evidence of exploitation in the wild. Two dates are worth keeping apart: CISA updated the long-standing advisory ICSA-25-135-18 on 15 September to add the SINEMA Remote Connect Edge Client and the vendor fixes — an advisory update, not a new vulnerability — and this 18 September publication is the research behind it. The CVE identifiers in this set carry 2025 prefixes despite the 2026 disclosure, which is consistent with how the line was assigned but worth confirming against Siemens’ own advisory before you put them in a ticket. Our sector read: local processing engines and SINEMA remote access are used for edge processing and vendor connectivity at remote and unmanned sites, which is where root on an edge box buys the most. - Nozomi Networks Labs research reported by Industrial Cyber, with the related CISA advisory update to ICSA-25-135-18 of 15 Sep 2026; CVE identifiers to be confirmed against the Siemens advisory - Research published 18 Sep 2026; related CISA advisory update 15 Sep 2026

item.title: [Info] ENISA’s 2026 Threat Landscape: 60% of unauthorised access came through known vulnerabilities, and 73% of targeted organisations were NIS2 essential or important entities
item.category: Research — EU threat landscape report
item.description: ENISA published its Threat Landscape 2026 on 22 September, covering calendar year 2025. As reported by Industrial Cyber, it counts 4,709 hacktivist campaigns against EU member states, more than 89% of them DDoS. It finds that 60% of unauthorised-access incidents used known vulnerabilities and that 73% of targeted organisations were classed as essential or important entities under EU rules. It records more than 48,000 new vulnerabilities, 22% more than the year before. Of state-nexus activity, 47.6% was Russia-nexus and 15.5% China-nexus. The coverage reviewed gives no energy or oil and gas breakdown, so no sector-specific figure is quoted here. Two points still apply to EU oil and gas operators, most of whom are NIS2 entities. The main way in is still a known, unpatched flaw, which is the same pattern as this edition’s KEV cards. And hacktivist activity against the EU is overwhelmingly DDoS, which argues for keeping public-facing and OT-dependent services apart. - ENISA Threat Landscape 2026, figures as reported by Industrial Cyber; the ENISA report itself was not directly reviewed; oil and gas application is editorial assessment - Published 22 Sep 2026; covers 2025

item.title: [Critical] Ivanti Connect Secure: a three-flaw chain gave attackers root on fully patched VPNs — two flaws fixed under CVE-2026-104935, in KEV due 16 October; the third has no patch
item.category: Critical Advisory — Exploited VPN zero-day chain, CISA KEV; one link still unpatched
item.description: Ivanti disclosed on 13 October that a limited number of Connect Secure customers had been attacked through a chain of three flaws that gives an unauthenticated attacker root on a fully patched appliance. Two of them — an authentication bypass by spoofing and a file write that together allow unauthenticated command execution — are fixed under a single CVE, CVE-2026-104935, which Ivanti scores CVSS v3.1 8.6; the fixed releases are 22.8R2.5, 25.1.1.2, 25.1.3.0 and 25.1.3.1. The third, a privilege-escalation bug in an internal broker service, has no CVE and no patch yet; Ivanti expects a fix in the coming weeks. Volexity found the chain during an incident response and tracks the actor as UTA0576, a new name. Its case began on 3 October on a fully patched appliance, and Defused saw activity from 1 October, so exploitation dates from at least early October. The intruders left no web shell or backdoor. They ran commands through the exploit itself, took domain credentials stored on the appliance, queried Active Directory for LAPS passwords and BitLocker recovery keys, Kerberoasted, sprayed passwords, sniffed LDAP traffic and wiped logs. Volexity and CISA warn that Ivanti’s Integrity Checker Tool may not detect this compromise because the chain alters code in memory, so a clean result is not proof. CISA added the CVE to KEV on 13 October with a 16 October deadline. Volexity has only low confidence that the motive is criminal rather than espionage. No oil and gas victim has been named. The sector read is ours: Connect Secure is a common front door for engineers and vendors into OT DMZs, and this chain hands an outsider the domain credentials behind it. - Ivanti advisory for CVE-2026-104935 and Volexity research (13 Oct 2026), as reported by SecurityWeek, CyberScoop and Cybersecurity Dive; Defused observations via Cybersecurity Dive; CISA KEV entry; OT remote-access relevance is editorial assessment - Exploitation from at least early October 2026; disclosed and added to KEV 13 Oct 2026; federal deadline 16 Oct 2026

item.title: [Critical] BeyondTrust Remote Support zero-day exploited since late August by a suspected China-nexus espionage group, Google says — patched 8 October, not yet in KEV
item.category: Critical Advisory — Remote-support appliance zero-day exploited by a suspected PRC-nexus espionage actor; not yet in KEV
item.description: Google Threat Intelligence Group reported on 15 October that CVE-2026-102764, a flaw in BeyondTrust Remote Support, was exploited as a zero-day from late August, and attributes the activity to ARMORY CASTLE, a suspected PRC-nexus espionage actor formerly tracked as UNC5221, on the strength of tooling and technique overlap. The flaw is improper validation of message origins in Remote Support’s internal messaging, which lets an attacker carry out file operations on the appliance; BeyondTrust scores it CVSS v4.0 9.3, and every Remote Support release up to 26.2.3 is affected. SecurityWeek reports that two appliances were compromised, one hosted by BeyondTrust and one self-hosted. The intruders gained root, installed a PHP web shell GTIG calls SAWFLY and a SOCKS5 tunneller it calls BARECLAW, harvested credentials, deleted logs and used the product’s own file-transfer feature to pull documents from user desktops. BeyondTrust identified the defect on 28 September, shipped patch BT26-05-RS on 8 October for releases 24.3.1 to 26.2.3, and had patched all SaaS customers by 9 October; self-hosted appliances without automatic updates must be patched by hand, and releases older than 24.3.1 must upgrade first. GTIG names no victims or sectors and advises treating any internet-reachable appliance that ran a vulnerable release during the window as potentially compromised. The CVE was not in KEV as of CISA’s 15 October catalog. The sector read is ours: remote-support tools are how many IT help desks, OEMs and integrators reach operator stations and engineering PCs, so a compromised support appliance is a ready-made path to the plant side. - Google Threat Intelligence Group blog (15 Oct 2026); BeyondTrust advisory BT26-05; compromise and timeline details as reported by SecurityWeek and The Record (16 Oct 2026); CVSS from the CVE record; OT relevance is editorial assessment - Exploited from late August 2026; defect identified 28 Sep; fix shipped 8 Oct, SaaS patched 9 Oct; disclosed 15 Oct 2026

item.title: [Critical] Citrix NetScaler: a fourth critical flaw (CVSS 9.5) follows three exploited ones — and builds that fixed the zero-days stay exposed when used as a SAML identity provider
item.category: Critical Advisory — Remote-access gateway; three exploited flaws in CISA KEV and a fourth critical flaw patched 8 Oct
item.description: On 8 October Citrix published bulletin CTX697191 for CVE-2026-107406, a memory overflow in NetScaler ADC and Gateway appliances configured as a SAML service provider or identity provider, which Citrix says may lead to remote code execution or denial of service. It is scored CVSS v4.0 9.5, has no workaround, and Citrix says it is not aware of exploitation; it was not in KEV as of CISA’s 15 October catalog. The catch is that builds which fixed the late-September zero-days — 14.1-73.37 to 73.41 and 13.1-64.23 to 64.28 — remain vulnerable when the appliance acts as a SAML identity provider, and older builds are vulnerable in either role, so many sites must upgrade again, to 14.1-73.46 or 13.1-64.29 and later (13.1-37.283 for FIPS and NDcPP). The three earlier flaws are confirmed exploited and in KEV. CVE-2026-88771, unauthenticated command execution, and CVE-2026-88772, a memory overflow that needs DTLS (on by default on VPN virtual servers), both CVSS v4 9.5, were patched and listed on 27 September. CVE-2026-88779, a SAML memory overflow scored 8.7, was patched on 3 October and listed on 4 October; Citrix and watchTowr describe it as a crash bug, and CISA has warned it is used to force reboots so that code planted through 88771 runs. CISA has renewed its call to patch and released Sigma detection rules. Google Threat Intelligence and LevelBlue describe what intruders leave behind: a PHP web shell (WHIPSHOT), a Python tunneller (SLAPSHOT), a rogue superuser account named sec_monitor and stolen configuration archives. Mandiant describes dozens of victim organisations across North America and Europe and suspected state-nexus actors, unnamed; Arctic Wolf counts at least 78 targeted organisations, which is not a count of confirmed compromises; Shadowserver sees more than 20,000 exposed or potentially vulnerable appliances. Upgrading does not remove an intruder who is already in. No oil and gas victim has been named. The sector read is ours: NetScaler Gateway is a common front door for vendor and engineer remote access into refinery, gas-plant and pipeline OT DMZs. - Citrix bulletins CTX697096, CTX697174 and CTX697191; CISA KEV entries and alerts; CVE-2026-107406 record and fixed builds via CIRCL Vulnerability-Lookup and The Hacker News (9 Oct 2026); CISA’s renewed warning via Cybersecurity Dive (12 Oct 2026); post-exploitation findings from Google Threat Intelligence and LevelBlue; victim and exposure counts from Mandiant, Arctic Wolf and Shadowserver; OT remote-access relevance is editorial assessment - Two zero-days patched and added to KEV 27 Sep 2026; third flaw patched 3 Oct, added to KEV 4 Oct; fourth flaw disclosed 8 Oct 2026; CISA renewed its patch call, reported 12 Oct 2026

item.title: [Critical] KEV, 13–15 October: an exploited PAN-OS root flaw, a CVSS 9.8 Cisco email-gateway bug and the Windows zero-day from Patch Tuesday, all on three-day deadlines
item.category: Critical Advisory — CISA KEV additions 13–15 Oct: boundary firewall, mail gateway and Windows zero-days
item.description: CISA added seven CVEs to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog between 13 and 15 October; Ivanti’s has its own card. The one closest to OT is CVE-2026-0322 in Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS, added on 14 October: an attacker with credentials and network access to the management interface of a PA-Series or VM-Series firewall or Panorama can run code as root. Palo Alto, which found it internally, reports very limited exploitation, scores it CVSS v4.0 8.6 and lists fixed releases including 12.2.4, 12.1.10-h2, 11.2.16, 11.1.16-h3 and 10.2.18-h12; Prisma Access and Cloud NGFW are not affected. Also on 14 October came CVE-2026-76519 in Cisco Secure Email Gateway, CVSS 9.8: a sender with no login can write files and reach root through a crafted attachment where File Reputation is enabled on a mail policy and Content Scanner Tools are older than 25.3.0.5525. Cisco is aware of attacks this month; the fixes are AsyncOS 15.5.5-014 or 16.5.0-780 (the 16.0 train must migrate) or the Content Scanner Tools update. It is separate from CVE-2026-76461, a SQL-injection flaw in the same gateway that was exploited and added to KEV in September. On 13 October CISA listed CVE-2026-96951, a Windows Shell security-feature bypass (CVSS 8.8) that Microsoft’s October update fixed among more than 1,400 CVEs; SecurityWeek describes it as a Mark-of-the-Web bypass that needs a user to open a file. The rest were AhsayCBS backup-server flaws CVE-2026-105133 and -105134 (14 October) and Atlassian Data Center CVE-2026-21589 (15 October). Deadlines run from 16 to 18 October. No victims or actors are named for any of them. The sector read is ours: PAN-OS firewalls commonly sit at refinery and pipeline IT/OT boundaries, and Windows engineering workstations and HMIs are where a mail-borne file ends up. - CISA KEV catalog (version 2026.10.15); Palo Alto Networks advisory for CVE-2026-0322; Cisco advisory cisco-sa-esa-afw-zqYJkjxp as reported by The Hacker News and SecurityWeek; Microsoft’s October 2026 release as reported by SecurityWeek; oil and gas relevance is editorial assessment - KEV additions 13, 14 and 15 Oct 2026; deadlines 16–18 Oct 2026

item.title: [High] SonicWall SMA1000: a CVSS 10 pre-authentication flaw drew exploitation attempts two days after the fix — no confirmed breach, not in KEV
item.category: Critical Advisory — Remote-access appliance, maximum-severity pre-authentication flaw; exploitation attempts reported; not in KEV
item.description: SonicWall published advisory SNWLID-2026-0017 on 6 October for CVE-2026-102255, a server-side request forgery in the Work Place interface of its SMA1000 remote-access appliances that it rates maximum severity; CISA’s enrichment scores it CVSS v3.1 10.0. Through an unintended alternate access path, an unauthenticated attacker can make the appliance send requests to its own internal functions. Affected are the SMA 6210, 7210 and 8200v on 12.4.3-03526 or older and 12.5.0-02952 or older; the fixes are 12.4.3-03670 and 12.5.0-03082, and there is no workaround. The same release fixes three flaws that need authentication: an OS command injection (CVE-2026-102256), a Zip Slip in the Appliance Management Console (CVE-2026-102257) and stored cross-site scripting (CVE-2026-102258). SMA 100 appliances and firewall SSL VPN are not affected. Defused saw its first hits on SMA decoys on 8 October and Previdian counted 135 attempts from two US addresses; reporting so far describes attempts, not successful break-ins, and the flaw was not in KEV as of CISA’s 15 October catalog. SMA1000 has been a repeated target this year, including zero-days exploited in June. No oil and gas victim is named. The sector read is ours: SMA1000 appliances broker vendor and contractor access into industrial networks, and a pre-authentication flaw on that broker is a direct line toward the OT DMZ. - SonicWall advisory SNWLID-2026-0017 and the CVE record (CISA-ADP CVSS); exploitation attempts as reported by SecurityWeek, The Hacker News and Dark Reading (12 Oct 2026); OT remote-access relevance is editorial assessment - Fix published 6 Oct 2026; attempts observed from 8 Oct 2026; reported 12 Oct 2026

item.title: [High] Schneider Electric: Sage RTUs do not properly verify firmware authenticity — and Pro-face and Harmony STW6 HMIs carry an 8.8 flaw triggered from a web page
item.category: Critical Advisory — SCADA RTU firmware authenticity and HMI component flaws; Schneider Electric October notices; not exploited
item.description: Schneider Electric issued two new security notices on 13 October. SEVD-2026-286-02 covers its Sage remote terminal units — the 1410, 1430, 1450, 2400, 3030 Magnum and 4400 — which do not sufficiently verify that firmware is authentic. Under CVE-2026-102250, modified firmware can be loaded when an authorised administrator starts an update; Schneider scores it CVSS v3.1 7.2 (v4.0 8.6) with high privileges required, and the fix is firmware C3414-500-S02L0. SEVD-2026-286-01 covers Pro-face STW6000 and Harmony STW6 HMIs, all versions, where an unmaintained third-party component could let an attacker take control of the device if a user visits a malicious web page; CVE-2026-96434 scores CVSS v3.1 8.8 and needs that user interaction. Schneider also reissued an older Altivar drive notice (SEVD-2025-252-01, version 5.0) the same day. Neither new flaw is in KEV and no exploitation is reported. The sector read is ours, and this one sits close to the sector: Sage RTUs are a long-standing choice for pipeline, gas-measurement and utility telemetry, so the realistic attack is a tampered firmware file reaching a technician’s laptop before an update visit — which makes the provenance of firmware as important as the patch. - Schneider Electric security notices SEVD-2026-286-01 and SEVD-2026-286-02 (13 Oct 2026), with CVE records via CIRCL Vulnerability-Lookup; oil and gas deployment context is editorial assessment - Published 13 Oct 2026

item.title: [High] October OT Patch Tuesday: S7-1500 web-server flaws at CVSS 9.6 with no fix yet, an Industrial Edge path traversal, and an ArmorBlock password takeover
item.category: Critical Advisory — October OT Patch Tuesday: Siemens S7-1500, Industrial Edge and CROSSBOW, Rockwell ArmorBlock; several fixes not yet available; not exploited
item.description: Siemens released its October advisories on 13 October; SecurityWeek counts 17. Three matter most for process plants. SSA-591731 covers eight web-server flaws (CVE-2026-63350 to -63357) in S7-1500, ET 200SP, ET 200pro and Drive Controller CPUs, all versions, that could let an attacker run code in an authorised user’s browser and carry out PLC operations with that user’s rights; Siemens scores the advisory CVSS v3.1 9.6 and has no fix yet, only mitigations. SSA-784472 lists 377 CVEs, up to CVSS 10.0, in the optional Linux subsystem of the S7-1500 TM MFP technology module — the module, not the CPUs — again with no fix yet. SSA-832641 is an authenticated path traversal in Industrial Edge devices and some HMI panels (CVE-2026-44415, CVSS 9.1), fixed for Edge devices, IoT2050 and IPCs but not yet for SCALANCE LPE9413/9433 or the affected panels. Siemens also fixed 11 flaws, up to CVSS 8.8, in RUGGEDCOM CROSSBOW in version 6.0. Rockwell’s only new advisory, SD1801, covers 1732E ArmorBlock I/O modules on 3.012 and earlier: CVE-2026-12655 (CVSS v3.1 9.1) lets an unauthenticated attacker change the web-server password and take over the module, and CVE-2026-12656 (7.5) is a traffic-flood denial of service that needs a power cycle to clear; 3.013 fixes both and there is no workaround. Nothing in the set is in KEV or reported exploited. The sector read is ours: S7-1500 controllers and ArmorBlock I/O arrive inside compressor packages, terminal loading systems and vendor skids, which is where version tracking tends to fail. - Siemens ProductCERT advisories SSA-591731, SSA-784472, SSA-832641 and SSA-508506; Rockwell Automation advisory SD1801; advisory count per SecurityWeek’s 14 Oct 2026 roundup; oil and gas deployment context is editorial assessment - Siemens and Rockwell advisories 13 Oct 2026; SecurityWeek roundup 14 Oct 2026

item.title: [High] CISA: an authorisation flaw in Inductive Automation Ignition lets users escalate their privileges — CVSS 8.8, fixed in 8.1.55 and 8.3.9
item.category: Critical Advisory — SCADA/HMI platform privilege escalation; CISA ICS advisory; not exploited
item.description: CISA published ICSA-26-286-01 on 13 October for Inductive Automation’s Ignition SCADA and HMI platform. CVE-2026-92817 is an incorrect-authorisation flaw that allows privilege escalation, scored CVSS v3.1 8.8 (v4.0 8.7). Ignition 8.1.0 to 8.1.54 and 8.3.0 to 8.3.8 are affected, and 8.1.55 and 8.3.9 fix it. CISA reports no known public exploitation, the flaw is not in KEV, and the advisory lists the Critical Manufacturing, Energy and Information Technology sectors. It was one of two advisories CISA issued that day; the other covered a consumer Wi-Fi camera. The sector read is ours: Ignition is widely used for production monitoring, pipeline and gathering-system SCADA, terminal HMIs and the dashboards that pull data from all three, and privilege escalation on a SCADA gateway is how a stolen low-level login becomes more control than it should ever have had. - CISA ICS advisory ICSA-26-286-01 (CSAF record as indexed by CIRCL Vulnerability-Lookup), corroborated by SecurityWeek; oil and gas deployment context is editorial assessment - Advisory published 13 Oct 2026

item.title: [High] A second critical lwIP flaw in two weeks: CISA flags a CVSS 9.8 buffer overflow in the SMTP client, after September’s MQTT client bug — exposure depends on each device vendor
item.category: Critical Advisory — Embedded TCP/IP stack; two critical client flaws in two weeks; exposure set by each device vendor
item.description: CISA published ICSA-26-279-02 on 6 October for the SMTP client in lwIP 2.2.1, the lightweight open-source TCP/IP stack built into many controllers, gateways and sensors. CVE-2026-15340 is a classic buffer overflow that the advisory scores CVSS v3.1 9.8 (v4.0 9.3 in the CVE record). The fix is an upstream patch and commit rather than a new release, and CISA lists the Energy and Water and Wastewater sectors. It follows ICSA-26-265-01 of 22 September for lwIP’s MQTT client, CVE-2026-87121, an out-of-bounds write also scored 9.8 that may allow full code execution on the device; that batch also carried a second lwIP advisory, six Siemens republications and OpenPLC Runtime v3. Neither lwIP flaw is reported exploited or listed in KEV. Both sit in optional client applications inside a library, so whether a given RTU, flow computer, gas detector or wireless gateway is affected depends on whether its maker built in the SMTP or MQTT client — something only the device vendors can answer. Devices that email alarms or reports, or publish telemetry over MQTT, are the ones to ask about first. - CISA ICS advisories ICSA-26-279-02 (6 Oct 2026) and ICSA-26-265-01 to -09 (22 Sep 2026), via CIRCL Vulnerability-Lookup and CISA’s CSAF files; CVSS per the advisories and CVE records; oil and gas relevance is editorial assessment - MQTT client advisory 22 Sep 2026; SMTP client advisory 6 Oct 2026

item.title: [Critical] CISA: ten flaws, led by a CVSS 10.0 file-exposure bug, in Toptech TMS7 and TopHAT, terminal management software for midstream fuel terminals — fixed in 7.8, not exploited
item.category: Critical Advisory — Fuel and bulk-liquid terminal management software
item.description: CISA published ICSA-26-272-02 on 29 September for Toptech Systems TMS7 and TopHAT version 7.6.3. It lists ten vulnerabilities. The most serious, CVE-2026-71379, leaves files or directories accessible to external parties and is scored CVSS v3.1 10.0 (v4 10.0). CVE-2026-70356 allows unrestricted upload of a dangerous file type (v3.1 9.1), and five SQL injection flaws — CVE-2026-72510, CVE-2026-63713, CVE-2026-68954, CVE-2026-68068 and CVE-2026-72507 — score v3.1 9.0. The rest are a session fixation flaw (v3.1 7.1) and two low-scoring eval-injection and cross-site scripting issues. CISA says successful exploitation could let an attacker access critical data or execute arbitrary code, lists the Energy, Chemical and Transportation Systems sectors, and says the products are deployed worldwide. The fix is release 7.8, which Toptech issued on 20 July with a customer advisory, so sites still on 7.6.3 have had a fix available for more than two months. No known public exploitation has been reported to CISA, and none of the flaws is in KEV. This one is squarely in the sector: Toptech, part of IDEX, describes itself as providing batch controller hardware and terminal management solutions for the midstream oil and gas industry, and TMS7 is part of its terminal management line. In a fuel or bulk-liquid terminal, software of this class typically authorises drivers and carriers, allocates product, produces bills of lading, keeps inventory and talks to the batch controllers at the loading rack (that description is ours, not CISA’s). A database or file-system compromise there is a commercial and operational problem even if no controller is touched. - CISA ICS advisory ICSA-26-272-02 (CSAF record as indexed by CIRCL Vulnerability-Lookup); fix date per CISA; product and company description from Toptech’s website; the terminal-function description is editorial - Fix released 20 Jul 2026; CISA advisory published 29 Sep 2026

item.title: [Critical] An exploited FortiMail flaw lets an unauthenticated attacker write files on the mail gateway — in KEV since 1 October, and Fortinet’s 5 October update lists fixed releases
item.category: Critical Advisory — Exploited email security gateway, CISA KEV
item.description: Fortinet published FG-IR-26-175 on 1 October for CVE-2026-104286, a path traversal flaw combined with improper NULL-byte handling in FortiMail. Fortinet says it lets an unauthenticated attacker “write arbitrary files on the underlying system via crafted HTTP or HTTPS requests”, scores it CVSS 9.8 and says it has been reported exploited in the wild; Fortinet found the flaw internally. CISA added it to KEV the same day with a 4 October federal deadline. Affected branches are 7.2.0 to 7.2.9, 7.4.0 to 7.4.8, 7.6.0 to 7.6.6 and 8.0.0 to 8.0.1. When the advisory first appeared the fixed releases were listed as planned, with no date. Fortinet’s 5 October update now lists 7.4.9, 7.6.7 and 8.0.2 or later, and tells 7.2 users to move to the 7.4 branch or above. Its workarounds still matter until each unit is upgraded: disable Identity-Based Encryption (IBE), restrict webmail access from untrusted networks, and use web application firewall rules to block path-traversal requests to the IBE endpoint. No actor, campaign or victim has been disclosed. The sector read is ours: a mail gateway is not OT, but in oil and gas it is the relay for vendor advisories, nominations and scheduling, and the alarm and production-report email that leaves plant networks, and a file-write foothold on it is a trusted position next to the systems the business side of operations depends on. - Fortinet PSIRT advisory FG-IR-26-175 and its 5 Oct solution update; CISA KEV entry; launch-day fix status as reported by SecurityWeek; oil and gas relevance is editorial assessment - Advisory and KEV addition 1 Oct 2026 (due 4 Oct); fixed releases listed 5 Oct 2026

item.title: [Critical] Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager: an exploited authentication bypass gives unauthenticated attackers admin-level API access to the system that configures every site — CVSS 9.8, in KEV since 30 September
item.category: Critical Advisory — Exploited SD-WAN management controller, CISA KEV
item.description: Cisco disclosed CVE-2026-76504 on 30 September. Improper handling of URI encoding in Catalyst SD-WAN Manager lets a remote, unauthenticated request get past an authentication rule meant to restrict a specific API endpoint, giving administrator-level access. Cisco scores it CVSS 9.8, says there are no workarounds, and states that its PSIRT “became aware of active exploitation of this vulnerability” in September 2026. CISA added it to KEV on 30 September with a 3 October deadline, and Cisco revised the advisory to version 1.1 on 2 October. Fixed releases are 20.9.10.1, 20.12.8.2, 20.15.6.1, 20.18.4.1, 26.1.2.1 and 26.2.1; releases older than 20.9 must migrate to a fixed release. BleepingComputer counts it as the fifth exploited Catalyst SD-WAN zero-day of 2026. No actor or victim has been named. The sector read is ours: where SD-WAN carries traffic between control centres, compressor and pump stations, terminals and field offices, the manager is the system that pushes configuration and policy to every edge router, so admin access to it is a route to changing segmentation at every site at once. It is the same exposure as the exploited Arista VeloCloud orchestrator in KEV since 22 September (see Arista VeloCloud). - Cisco security advisory cisco-sa-sdwan-webauth-xr8beuuU (v1.1); CISA KEV entry; zero-day count per BleepingComputer; oil and gas WAN relevance is editorial assessment - Advisory and KEV addition 30 Sep 2026 (due 3 Oct); advisory revised 2 Oct 2026

item.title: [Critical] MikroTik RouterOS: the exploited “MikroTrick” chain is fully in KEV, and CISA now flags a separate pre-authentication CVSS 9.8 web-management flaw that is not — the routers at remote sites
item.category: Critical Advisory — Confirmed exploited, remote-site edge routers, CISA KEV
item.description: CISA added CVE-2026-67279 in MikroTik RouterOS to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 25 September, with a federal remediation deadline of 28 September. It is an SSH workflow flaw that, in the KEV entry’s words, “could allow an unauthenticated client to open a session channel and send an exec request”, and that can be chained for unauthenticated exploitation of CVE-2026-86060; reporting gives it CVSS 6.9 without stating the version. It joins CVE-2026-86060, an argument-injection flaw, and CVE-2026-67277, a missing-authentication flaw in the bandwidth-test service, both added to KEV on 10 September. CERT Polska reported on 5 September that a two-flaw SSH chain it calls “MikroTrick” has been exploited in the wild since about 2 September. Its 22 September technical analysis names the chain: CVE-2026-67279 combined with CVE-2026-86060, which gives an unauthenticated attacker full administrative control. CVE-2026-67276, which an earlier edition of this card placed in the chain, is not in KEV. CERT Polska lists RouterOS 7.24.2, 7.23.4 and 6.49.21 as fixed; a related flaw, CVE-2026-67278, needs 7.24.3 or 7.23.6 because the earlier fix was incomplete. Separately, CISA’s ICS advisory ICSA-26-272-06 of 29 September covers CVE-2026-84411, a pre-authentication integer underflow in RouterOS web management that can lead to code execution or denial of service, scored CVSS v3.1 9.8 and fixed in RouterOS 7.24 and later; no exploitation has been reported and it is not in KEV. Shadowserver counted more than 122,500 MikroTik devices with SSH reachable from the internet in early September — an exposure count, not a count of compromised or unpatched devices. No victims or sectors have been named, so there is no confirmed oil and gas victim. The sector read is ours: inexpensive, capable routers are a common contractor choice for cellular and fixed-wireless backhaul at wellpads, tank batteries, remote valve and meter stations and pipeline block-valve sites — often the one device on site with a route to both the SCADA host and the internet. - CISA KEV catalog entries of 10 and 25 Sep 2026; CERT Polska posts of 5 Sep 2026 and its 22 Sep 2026 technical analysis naming the chain; CVE-2026-67279 KEV addition and CVSS as reported by The Hacker News; Shadowserver exposure count as reported in early September. No victims or sectors named; oil and gas deployment context is editorial assessment; CISA ICS advisory ICSA-26-272-06 for CVE-2026-84411 - Exploitation observed from about 2 Sep 2026; CERT Polska posts 5 Sep 2026; KEV additions 10 Sep 2026 and 25 Sep 2026 (due 28 Sep 2026); CISA ICS advisory for CVE-2026-84411 29 Sep 2026

item.title: [Medium] Lantronix G520 cellular gateways do not properly verify software signatures — CISA says an attacker could replace the software and run code as root; fixed in 2.6.0.7R6
item.category: Critical Advisory — Cellular gateway for remote sites; software signature check
item.description: CISA published ICSA-26-272-01 on 29 September for the Lantronix G520 Series cellular gateway, version 2.6.0.4R6_stable. CVE-2026-91191 is an improper verification of a cryptographic signature and CVE-2026-84409 is a cross-site scripting flaw; each is scored CVSS v3.1 7.5 (v4 7.7). CISA says successful exploitation could allow an attacker to “replace software and execute arbitrary code with root privileges”. It lists the Energy, Water and Wastewater, and Transportation Systems sectors, with deployment worldwide. Lantronix release 2.6.0.7R6 fixes both. No known public exploitation has been reported to CISA, and neither flaw is in KEV. The sector read is ours: industrial cellular gateways like this are how many wellpads, tank batteries, meter stations and cathodic-protection sites get RTU and flow-computer data back to SCADA, and a gateway that will accept replaced software is a root foothold on the one device that bridges the site to the carrier network. It is the same remote-site edge question as the exploited MikroTik routers above, without the exploitation. - CISA ICS advisory ICSA-26-272-01 (CSAF record as indexed by CIRCL Vulnerability-Lookup); oil and gas deployment context is editorial assessment - Advisory published 29 Sep 2026

item.title: [Critical] Arista’s VeloCloud SD-WAN orchestrator, a CVSS 10 flaw, is being exploited — the system that pushes configuration to your remote sites. F5 BIG-IP APM joins it in KEV
item.category: Critical Advisory — Exploited SD-WAN orchestrator and access gateway, CISA KEV
item.description: Arista Security Advisory 0183 (22 September) covers CVE-2026-93952 in the on-premises VeloCloud Orchestrator (VCO), CVSS v3.1 10.0. Improper input validation lets an attacker reach privileged internal VCO functions without VCO tenant or operator credentials. Arista says it is “known to be actively exploited”. The flaw is exposed where certificate-based Edge-to-VCO authentication is configured. Hosted VCO is already patched. Fixes are 5.2.3.16 or later and 6.4.2.8 or later; Arista lists no fix yet for the 6.1.x and 7.0.x trains. Its indicators include files named .vcnode.js and vc-sysmond, an x-vc-opt HTTP header and source addresses 142.93.149.77 and 104.248.126.159. Its interim advice is to restrict the VCO web interface to trusted networks. CISA added the flaw to KEV on 22 September alongside F5 BIG-IP APM CVE-2026-94127, CVSS v3.1 9.8 (v4.0 9.3). That is an unauthenticated heap overflow, exploitable only where a virtual server carries both an APM access policy and an OAuth authorization-server profile; F5 advisory K000162605 lists engineering hotfixes, and CISA’s KEV entry advises applying F5’s iRule first to allow forensic triage, then patching. Both were due 25 September, and the two Check Point flaws in the same batch have their own cards. SD-WAN is a common way to connect compressor and pump stations, terminals and field offices, and whoever controls the orchestrator controls the configuration of every edge it manages. No oil and gas victim has been named for either flaw. - Arista Security Advisory 0183 and F5 advisory K000162605, with exploitation detail from Rapid7 and SecurityWeek; CISA KEV additions of 22 Sep 2026 as reported by SecurityAffairs and Help Net Security; oil and gas deployment context is editorial assessment - Advisories and KEV additions 22 Sep 2026; Arista advisory rev 1.1 (23 Sep) added only a CSAF file; federal deadline 25 Sep 2026 reached

item.title: [Critical] A second Check Point management-server flaw was a zero-day for two months — attacked in July, fixed and added to KEV on 22 September
item.category: Critical Advisory — Firewall management server, zero-day exploited, CISA KEV
item.description: Check Point disclosed CVE-2026-93616 on 22 September; neither the vendor nor CISA has published a CVSS score. It is a pre-authentication path traversal in the Security Management web service that lets a remote attacker run scripts and load Java classes on the server. Check Point says it saw a “handful of pinpointed attacks on July 23, 2026”, so the flaw was exploited about two months before a fix shipped on 22 September. Reporting lists Security Management Server, Multi-Domain Security Management, Log Server, Multi-Domain Log Server and SmartEvent as affected; advisory sk1000171 lists the fixed builds. CISA added it to KEV on 22 September with a federal deadline of 25 September. No actor or victim has been named. This is not CVE-2026-91843, the over-long-username flaw fixed on 17 September, which remains unexploited. The management server writes policy for every gateway it controls, including those at the IT/OT boundary of refineries, gas plants and pipeline control centres. A compromise dating back to July would not be removed by the 22 September fix. - Check Point security advisory (22 Sep 2026) and sk1000171; affected-product list per Help Net Security and SecurityAffairs; CISA KEV addition of 22 Sep 2026 as reported by those outlets; oil and gas deployment context is editorial assessment - Attacks observed 23 Jul 2026; fix, disclosure and KEV addition 22 Sep 2026; federal deadline 25 Sep 2026 reached

item.title: [Medium] One unauthenticated packet can crash TDengine, the time-series database some operators use behind telemetry and SCADA data — CVSS 7.5, fixed in 3.4.1.6, not exploited
item.category: Critical Advisory — Industrial time-series database, unauthenticated denial of service
item.description: Ridge Security disclosed CVE-2026-42542 on 23 September, a pre-authentication flaw in the RPC service of the open-source TDengine time-series database, which listens on TCP port 6030 by default. The vendor’s GitHub advisory, GHSA-vg95-j2hf-hvjx, describes an integer underflow in the uvConnMayGetUserInfo() function: a client-supplied message length is not validated, the calculation wraps around, and the resulting oversized memory copy crashes the taosd server process. No credentials or session are needed; a single crafted packet is enough. It is rated CVSS 7.5 (High), availability impact only. Affected are TDengine 3.4.0.0 through 3.4.1.5; the fix is 3.4.1.6. Ridge confirms remote denial of service, says plainly that it is not claiming code execution, and reports no telemetry of in-the-wild exploitation and no known public exploit code. Ridge names industrial telemetry, energy, utilities and factory-floor SCADA among the settings where TDengine runs. Its place on this page is editorial assessment: where a time-series store sits behind production, pipeline or compression telemetry, losing it blinds trending, alarm analytics and reporting even though control keeps running. - TDengine GitHub security advisory GHSA-vg95-j2hf-hvjx and Ridge Security disclosure, both reviewed directly; reported by Industrial Cyber (25 Sep 2026); oil and gas applicability is editorial assessment - Fix released with vendor advisory 4 Jun 2026; researcher disclosure 23 Sep 2026

item.title: [Critical] Cisco’s 16 September hardening release follows a CVSS 10 FMC bypass exploited since August — root on the console that writes your IT/OT boundary rules
item.category: Critical Advisory — Exploited firewall management platform, CISA KEV
item.description: On 16 September Cisco published hardening release cisco-sa-hardening-asaftdfmc-uvpPROhN, covering eight internally found flaws across ASA, FTD and Secure Firewall Management Center (CVE-2026-20329 to CVE-2026-20336, maximum CVSS 9.9). It follows FMC flaws that were already under attack. Cisco and CISA confirmed on 9 September that CVE-2026-20079 in FMC is exploited in the wild: a CVSS 10.0 authentication bypass in which a remote, unauthenticated attacker sends crafted HTTP requests and gains root on the appliance. CISA added it to KEV that day with a federal remediation deadline of 12 September, now passed. Cisco Talos describes three post-compromise clusters. One used CVE-2026-20079 and is not attributed to anyone. A second, an APT cluster, combined it with CVE-2026-20316; Talos notes overlaps with a known group’s tooling but does not attribute the activity to that group. A third, which Talos assesses with high confidence to be a ransomware operator, got in only through CVE-2026-20316, a CVSS 5.3 static-credential flaw that is not in KEV, and went on to deploy ransomware. No OT impact and no oil and gas victim has been named. But FMC is where the firewall policy between corporate networks and plant, pipeline SCADA and terminal control networks is written, so root on FMC is the ability to quietly loosen that boundary. - Cisco hardening release cisco-sa-hardening-asaftdfmc-uvpPROhN (16 Sep 2026); Cisco security advisory update and Cisco Talos research of 9 Sep 2026, plus the CISA KEV addition — reported by SecurityWeek, cluster detail corroborated by The Hacker News; Talos does not attribute the clusters to named groups - Advisory updated and KEV listing added 9 Sep 2026; reporting 10 Sep 2026; federal deadline 12 Sep 2026; hardening release 16 Sep 2026

item.title: [High] CISA adds Zyxel GS1900 switches to KEV after one actor pulled configs and root credentials from nearly a thousand of them — the switch class that turns up at small stations and contractor sites
item.category: Critical Advisory — Exploited small-site managed switch, CISA KEV
item.description: CISA added CVE-2026-7273 to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 21 September with a federal remediation deadline of 24 September. It is a stack-based buffer overflow in the CGI program of Zyxel’s GS1900-series managed switches — GS1900-8, 8HP, 10HP, 16, 24, 24E, 24EP, 24HPv2, 48 and 48HPv2 — that lets an unauthenticated attacker with access to the management interface run operating-system commands through a crafted HTTP request. Zyxel patched it on 16 June in firmware 2.90(AAHH.2)C0 and the per-model equivalents, and gives no CVSS score, so we print none. GreyNoise’s report of the same day describes what it calls the first observed in-the-wild exploitation: a single actor, assessed by GreyNoise to be a Chinese speaker, compromised 996 GS1900 switches in 48 countries from on or about 17 August — Italy, the United States and Taiwan the largest shares — using an obfuscated Python tool that pulled device configurations and root-level password hashes over TFTP. GreyNoise says 564 of the victims were still on factory-default credentials. The same actor stole records from an unnamed western government organisation through two WordPress flaws and probed Gitea, UniFi, Proxmox and PAN-OS GlobalProtect; GreyNoise also assesses the actor as the same as, or related to, the group behind earlier Gitea exploitation, based on shared command-and-control infrastructure, malware and techniques — an assessment rather than an observation. No oil and gas victim is named and no OT impact is reported. The sector read is ours: GS1900 is an inexpensive managed switch, not industrial-rated, and it is exactly what a contractor or a small operator installs in a wellsite shelter, a meter station cabinet or a terminal office to hang cellular routers, cameras and an HMI PC off — the places where a device configuration in an attacker’s hands maps your remote-site network for them. - CISA KEV catalog addition (21 Sep 2026), Zyxel security advisory (16 Jun 2026) and GreyNoise research (21 Sep 2026); actor language and links to earlier activity are GreyNoise assessments; oil and gas deployment context is editorial assessment - Zyxel fix 16 Jun 2026; GreyNoise report and KEV addition 21 Sep 2026; federal deadline 24 Sep 2026

item.title: [Critical] Check Point’s gateway VPN flaw is now being exploited and is in KEV — the Dutch NCSC’s “imminent” warning came true within days
item.category: Critical Advisory — VPN gateway, exploited, CISA KEV
item.description: On 22 September Check Point updated its advisory for CVE-2026-85102: improper validation of certificate data during VPN negotiation that lets an unauthenticated attacker run code on Security Gateways and Spark firewalls. The company says that “starting September 12, 2026, we observed a wave of exploitation attempts against Spark customers.” It gives no customer count and no attribution. CISA added the flaw to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog the same day, with a federal remediation deadline of 25 September. Check Point published certificate indicators from the attempts: subjects CN=vpn, CN=vpn-user or CN=vpnuser, with OU=users and O=global. Fixes have been available since 9 September under sk1000117. The Dutch NCSC warned on 12 September that exploitation of this flaw and its sibling, CVE-2026-85103, was imminent. Only CVE-2026-85102 is in KEV and named as exploited; no exploitation of CVE-2026-85103 has been reported. Check Point also disclosed on 22 September that a different flaw, in its management server, had been attacked since July (see the separate card). Gateways of this class often sit at the IT/OT boundary of refineries, gas plants and pipeline control centres, and Spark appliances turn up at small remote sites. They terminate the vendor and contractor tunnels into those networks. - Check Point security advisory (22 Sep 2026) and sk1000117; CISA KEV addition of 22 Sep 2026 as reported by SecurityAffairs and Help Net Security; Dutch NCSC warning reported by BleepingComputer on 12 Sep 2026; oil and gas deployment context is editorial assessment - Fixes 9 Sep 2026; exploitation attempts observed from 12 Sep 2026; advisory updated and KEV addition 22 Sep 2026; federal deadline 25 Sep 2026 reached

item.title: [High] Check Point fixes a CVSS 9.8 pre-authentication root flaw in the servers that write your firewall policy — no exploitation reported
item.category: Critical Advisory — Firewall management server, pre-authentication RCE, not exploited
item.description: Check Point has fixed CVE-2026-91843, rated CVSS 9.8, in its Security Management and Log Servers, under advisory sk1000155, as reported by The Hacker News on 17 September and in SecurityWeek’s round-up. A stack overflow in the login process, triggered by an overly long username in an unauthenticated request, can give a remote attacker code execution as root. The Hacker News reports that a Trusted Clients misconfiguration is a precondition; that detail could not be confirmed in the vendor text, so check sk1000155 against your own configuration rather than relying on it. Reported affected versions are R82.10 up to Jumbo Hotfix Take 44, R82 up to Take 126, all builds of R82.20, R81.20 up to Take 166, R81.10 up to Take 190, and the end-of-support R81 and R80.x lines; Multi-Domain Server is affected and Smart-1 Cloud is already fixed. The fix is a LivePatch delivered through sk1000155. Check Point says there is “no indication that this vulnerability has been exploited in the wild.” This is separate from the VPN flaws the Dutch NCSC warned about on 12 September, and from CVE-2026-93616, a different management-server flaw that Check Point disclosed on 22 September as exploited (see the separate card). The management server is where policy for the gateways at the IT/OT boundary of refineries, gas plants and pipeline control centres is written, so root on it is the ability to change that boundary everywhere at once. - Check Point advisory sk1000155, as reported by The Hacker News and SecurityWeek; the vendor page itself was not directly reviewed - Reported 17 Sep 2026

item.title: [High] Rockwell revises its lock-out recovery notice a fifth time, adding Micro820 and Micro850 — the small controllers at wellsites and pump skids that attackers have been setting passwords on
item.category: Critical Advisory — Vendor hardening notice, revised after attackers locked operators out of exposed PLCs
item.description: Rockwell Automation published revision 5.0 of security notice SD1790, “Important Hardening Guidance for Rockwell Automation/Allen-Bradley Controllers and Instructions for Restoring Access When the Password Is Unknown”, on 18 September. First issued on 30 July alongside an FBI public service announcement, the notice describes threat actors remotely altering the configuration of internet-exposed programmable logic controllers, changing their IP addresses and setting passwords where none existed, so that operators lose access to their own equipment. Revision 2.0 added MicroLogix 1100 recovery steps in July; revision 4.0 in August clarified that setting a password alone is not a sufficient mitigation; revision 5.0 extends the recovery instructions and hardening guidance to Micro820 and Micro850 controllers alongside MicroLogix 1100 and 1400. There is no CVE, because there is no vulnerability: the activity works through internet exposure and missing or default credentials. The recommended actions are to remove controllers from the public internet, use a VPN for any remote access that is genuinely needed, isolate controllers behind firewalls on a separate OT network, set strong passwords and keep offline backups, monitor logs, keep firmware current and leave controllers in RUN mode so configuration cannot be changed remotely. The FBI announcement concerned water and wastewater; the sector link here is our assessment. MicroLogix and Micro800 controllers are the same low-cost class found at wellsite separators and chemical-injection skids, saltwater-disposal pumps, small compressor packages and tank-battery automation, often installed by a packager with a cellular modem and never surveyed again. Rockwell published no new product vulnerability advisories between 10 and 22 September. - Rockwell Automation security notice SD1790 revision 5.0, referencing the FBI public service announcement of 30 Jul 2026; oil and gas applicability is editorial assessment - Notice first published 30 Jul 2026; revision 5.0 published 18 Sep 2026

item.title: [Critical] A CVSS 10 authentication bypass in Cisco ISE is being exploited — the policy engine that decides who gets onto your network
item.category: Critical Advisory — Exploited network access control platform, CISA KEV
item.description: Cisco published advisory cisco-sa-ISE-ABP-VNSW7Tn5 on 16 September for CVE-2026-76460, a CVSS 10.0 authentication bypass in Cisco Identity Services Engine and ISE-PIC. An API endpoint with insufficient authentication lets a remote, unauthenticated attacker bypass the web-based management interface. Cisco states that its PSIRT is aware of active exploitation, and all versions are affected until patched: 3.1 Patch 12, 3.2 Patch 11, 3.3 Patch 12, 3.4 Patch 7 and 3.5 Patch 4 carry the fix. There are no workarounds; Cisco points to infrastructure ACLs restricting management traffic as the only mitigation. CISA added the CVE to KEV on 16 September with a three-day federal deadline of 19 September, which has now passed. On 21 September Singapore’s Cyber Security Agency issued its own alert, AL-2026-126, urging the same patching, and ISE 3.0 is end-of-life and must be migrated rather than patched. No actor has been named, no indicators beyond checking access logs for unfamiliar usernames have been published, and no critical-infrastructure targeting has been claimed. The sector relevance is our assessment: ISE is the NAC and 802.1X policy engine that, in many operators, decides which devices and which vendor sessions are allowed onto the industrial DMZ and the plant network. Administrative control of it is administrative control of your segmentation policy. - Cisco security advisory cisco-sa-ISE-ABP-VNSW7Tn5 and the CISA KEV catalog, reported by SecurityWeek and BleepingComputer - Advisory published 16 Sep 2026; KEV addition 16 Sep 2026, deadline 19 Sep 2026

item.title: [High] About 20 flaws in one shared IO-Link master firmware base hit three vendors at once — unauthenticated root at the field layer
item.category: Critical Advisory — Field-layer I/O, shared OEM firmware
item.description: CERT@VDE published three advisories on 16 September that carry the same CVE range, CVE-2026-27546 through CVE-2026-27565, across three different brands: VDE-2026-014 for Pepperl+Fuchs ICE2-* and ICE3-* models, VDE-2026-027 for Phoenix Contact IOL MA8 EIP DI8 and IOL MA8 PN DI8, and VDE-2026-028 for Carlo Gavazzi YL212 and YN115 units. One shared CVE set across three vendors points to a common OEM firmware base. The worst two are CVE-2026-27546, an authentication bypass at CVSS 9.8, and CVE-2026-27565, an OS command injection at CVSS 9.8 reachable over the network without authentication or user interaction; below them sit command-injection and local-file-inclusion flaws at 8.8, an authorisation bypass at 8.1, path traversal at 7.5 and information disclosure at 6.5. The outcome is unauthenticated root code execution on the device and theft of stored password hashes and SSH private keys. Firmware below 1.7.4 is affected and the advisories name 1.7.8 as fixed — confirm the exact build with your vendor. On 24 September Nozomi Networks Labs published its technical write-up of the Pepperl+Fuchs findings (VDE-2026-014), counting 19 CVEs on the ICE2-8IOL-K45P-RJ45 it tested and showing that, chained, they give an unauthenticated attacker root on the device and the ability to manipulate sensor and actuator data. No exploitation has been reported. IO-Link masters aggregate sensors and actuators onto EtherNet/IP and PROFINET segments; in oil and gas they usually arrive inside packaged equipment — metering and analyser cabinets, custody-transfer skids, vendor process packages — rather than in the main DCS I/O count, which is why they are easy to miss. - CERT@VDE advisories VDE-2026-014, VDE-2026-027 and VDE-2026-028; Nozomi Networks Labs technical write-up of VDE-2026-014; oil and gas deployment context is editorial assessment - Advisories published 16 Sep 2026; Nozomi write-up 24 Sep 2026

item.title: [Medium] Seven new CISA ICS advisories plus one update on 17 September — Hitachi Energy FACTS, three Schneider products, Mitsubishi GX Works3, ABB Edgenius and an ELD
item.category: Critical Advisory — CISA ICS advisory batch
item.description: CISA released eight ICS advisories on Thursday 17 September — seven new, ICSA-26-260-01 through -07, plus one update: Bransys ELD, Mitsubishi Electric GX Works3 and Motion Control Settings, Hitachi Energy FACTS Control Platform, Schneider Electric Modicon M340 controllers and communication modules, Schneider Electric NetBotz 5 (750 and 755), ABB Ability Edgenius, and Schneider Electric PowerChute Serial Shutdown. GX Works3 and Motion Control Settings carry CVE-2026-15688, an authentication algorithm flaw scored CVSS v3.1 8.8 and v4.0 8.7, affecting all versions and enabling local authentication bypass and tampering with control programs.
